metadataReview.note: The inherited start (24 July 67) fell after the inherited end (20 July 67). Josephus dates his entry into Jotapata to 21 Artemisius, counts a siege of forty-seven days and dates the capture to 1 Panemus in Nero’s thirteenth year. G. J. Goldberg’s chronology converts these to 8–10 June and 20 July 67. The start is corrected to month precision (June 67), because the conversion of Macedonian months is approximate and the source gives a range of days; the existing 20 July end is retained. The Wikipedia infobox gives 24 May, whereas its text says early June; that variant is not adopted. Pleiades locates ancient Iotapata at Tel Yodfat, where excavations have documented the siege of 67. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred, and the figures reported by Josephus are not adopted.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Pleiades place 678201 (Iotapata, also Jotapata and Yodfat) publishes reprPoint [35.2776164,32.83226775], based on its DARE location [35.2775,32.832222] (accuracy 10 m) and its OpenStreetMap location of Tel Yodfat [35.2777328,32.8323135] (accuracy 20 m). Rounded to [35.2776,32.8323]. This is a representative point for the hilltop town besieged in 67, not the Roman camp, the siege ramp or the cave where Josephus hid. The gazetteer accuracy values describe the digitised location, not the extent of the siege works.
